# External Libraries

import ComposeBuilder from '/docs/partials/_compose-builder.mdx';

:::info
Currently an external library can only belong to a single user which is selected when the library is initially created.
:::

External libraries track assets stored in the filesystem outside of Immich. When the external library is scanned, Immich will load videos and photos from disk and create the corresponding assets. These assets will then be shown in the main timeline, and they will look and behave like any other asset, including viewing on the map, adding to albums, etc. Later, if a file is modified outside of Immich, you need to scan the library for the changes to show up.

If an external asset is deleted from disk, Immich will move it to trash on rescan. To restore the asset, you need to restore the original file. After 30 days the file will be removed from trash, and any changes to metadata within Immich will be lost.

:::caution

If you add metadata to an external asset in any way (i.e. add it to an album or edit the description), that metadata is only stored inside Immich and will not be persisted to the external asset file. If you move an asset to another location within the library all such metadata will be lost upon rescan. This is because the asset is considered a new asset after the move. This is a known issue and will be fixed in a future release.

:::

:::caution

Due to aggressive caching it can take some time for a refreshed asset to appear correctly in the web view. You need to clear the cache in your browser to see the changes. This is a known issue and will be fixed in a future release. In Chrome, you need to open the developer console with F12, then reload the page with F5, and finally right click on the reload button and select "Empty Cache and Hard Reload".

:::

### Import Paths

External libraries use import paths to determine which files to scan. Each library can have multiple import paths so that files from different locations can be added to the same library. Import paths are scanned recursively, and if a file is in multiple import paths, it will only be added once. Each import file must be a readable directory that exists on the filesystem; the import path dialog will alert you of any paths that are not accessible.

If the import paths are edited in a way that an external file is no longer in any import path, it will be removed from the library in the same way a deleted file would. If the file is moved back to an import path, it will be added again as if it was a new file.

### Troubleshooting

Sometimes, an external library will not scan correctly. This can happen if Immich can't access the files. Here are some things to check:

- In the docker-compose file, are the volumes mounted correctly?
- Are the volumes also mounted to any worker containers?
- Are the import paths set correctly, and do they match the path set in docker-compose file?
- Make sure you don't use symlinks in your import libraries, and that you aren't linking across docker mounts.
- Are the permissions set correctly?
- Make sure you are using forward slashes (`/`) and not backward slashes.

To validate that Immich can reach your external library, start a shell inside the container. Run `docker exec -it immich_server bash` to a bash shell. If your import path is `/mnt/photos`, check it with `ls /mnt/photos`. If you are using a dedicated microservices container, make sure to add the same mount point and check for availability within the microservices container as well.

### Exclusion Patterns

By default, all files in the import paths will be added to the library. If there are files that should not be added, exclusion patterns can be used to exclude them. Exclusion patterns are glob patterns are matched against the full file path. If a file matches an exclusion pattern, it will not be added to the library. Exclusion patterns can be added in the Scan Settings page for each library.

Some basic examples:

- `**/*.tif` will exclude all files with the extension `.tif`
- `**/hidden.jpg` will exclude all files named `hidden.jpg`
- `**/Raw/**` will exclude all files in any directory named `Raw`
- `**/*.{tif,jpg}` will exclude all files with the extension `.tif` or `.jpg`

Note that `*` is a wildcard matching zero or more characters (i.e., withinin a filename or single directory name). `**` matches zero or more subdirectories, recursively. It also includes any/all files within a subdirectory, i.e., when used at the end of a pattern. For example, `**/exclude_me/**` will exclude all files in any directory named `exclude_me`, as well as all files in any subdirectories of `exclude_me`, recursively.

Special characters such as @ should be escaped, for instance:

- `**/\@eaDir/**` will exclude all files in any directory named `@eaDir`

:::info
Internally, Immich uses the [glob](https://www.npmjs.com/package/glob) package to process exclusion patterns, and sometimes those patterns are translated into [Postgres LIKE patterns](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/functions-matching.html). The intention is to support basic folder exclusions but we recommend against advanced usage since those can't reliably be translated to the Postgres syntax. Please refer to the [glob documentation](https://github.com/isaacs/node-glob#glob-primer) for a basic overview on glob patterns.
:::

### Automatic watching (EXPERIMENTAL)

This feature is considered experimental and for advanced users only. If enabled, it will allow automatic watching of the filesystem which means new assets are automatically imported to Immich without needing to rescan.

If your photos are on a network drive, automatic file watching likely won't work. In that case, you will have to rely on a [periodic library refresh](#set-custom-scan-interval) to pull in your changes.

#### Troubleshooting

If you encounter an `ENOSPC` error, you need to increase your file watcher limit. In sysctl, this key is called `fs.inotify.max_user_watches` and has a default value of 8192. Increase this number to a suitable value greater than the number of files you will be watching. Note that Immich has to watch all files in your import paths including any ignored files.

```
ERROR [LibraryService] Library watcher for library c69faf55-f96d-4aa0-b83b-2d80cbc27d98 encountered error: Error: ENOSPC: System limit for number of file watchers reached, watch '/media/photo.jpg'
```

In rare cases, the library watcher can hang, preventing Immich from starting up. In this case, disable the library watcher in the configuration file. If the watcher is enabled from within Immich, the app must be started without the microservices. Disable the microservices in the docker compose file, start Immich, disable the library watcher in the admin settings, close Immich, re-enable the microservices, and then Immich can be started normally.

### Nightly job

There is an automatic scan job that is scheduled to run once a day. Its schedule is configurable, see [Set Custom Scan Interval](#set-custom-scan-interval).

This job also cleans up any libraries stuck in deletion. It is possible to trigger the cleanup by clicking "Scan all libraries" in the library management page.

### Deleting a Library

When deleting an external library, all assets inside are immediately deleted along with the library. Note that while a library can take a long time to fully delete in the background, it is immediately removed from the library list. If the deletion process is interrupted (for example, due to server restart), it will be cleaned up in the next nightly cron job. The cleanup process can also be manually initiated by clicking the "Scan All Libraries" button in the library list.

# Hardware-Accelerated Machine Learning

import ComposeBuilder from '/docs/partials/_compose-builder.mdx';

This feature allows you to use a GPU to accelerate machine learning tasks, such as Smart Search and Facial Recognition, while reducing CPU load.
As this is a new feature, it is still experimental and may not work on all systems.

:::info
You do not need to redo any machine learning jobs after enabling hardware acceleration. The acceleration device will be used for any jobs that run after enabling it.
:::

## Supported Backends

- ARM NN (Mali)
- CUDA (NVIDIA GPUs with [compute capability](https://developer.nvidia.com/cuda-gpus) 5.2 or higher)
- ROCm (AMD GPUs)
- OpenVINO (Intel GPUs such as Iris Xe and Arc)
- RKNN (Rockchip)

## Limitations

- The instructions and configurations here are specific to Docker Compose. Other container engines may require different configuration.
- Only Linux and Windows (through WSL2) servers are supported.
- ARM NN is only supported on devices with Mali GPUs. Other Arm devices are not supported.
- Some models may not be compatible with certain backends. CUDA is the most reliable.
- Search latency isn't improved by ARM NN due to model compatibility issues preventing its use. However, smart search jobs do make use of ARM NN.

## Prerequisites

#### ARM NN

- Make sure you have the appropriate linux kernel driver installed
  - This is usually pre-installed on the device vendor's Linux images
- `/dev/mali0` must be available in the host server
  - You may confirm this by running `ls /dev` to check that it exists
- You must have the closed-source `libmali.so` firmware (possibly with an additional firmware file)
  - Where and how you can get this file depends on device and vendor, but typically, the device vendor also supplies these
  - The `hwaccel.ml.yml` file assumes the path to it is `/usr/lib/libmali.so`, so update accordingly if it is elsewhere
  - The `hwaccel.ml.yml` file assumes an additional file `/lib/firmware/mali_csffw.bin`, so update accordingly if your device's driver does not require this file
- Optional: Configure your `.env` file, see [environment variables](/install/environment-variables) for ARM NN specific settings
  - In particular, the `MACHINE_LEARNING_ANN_FP16_TURBO` can significantly improve performance at the cost of very slightly lower accuracy

#### CUDA

- The GPU must have compute capability 5.2 or greater.
- The server must have the official NVIDIA driver installed.
- The installed driver must be >= 545 (it must support CUDA 12.3).
- On Linux (except for WSL2), you also need to have [NVIDIA Container Toolkit][nvct] installed.

#### ROCm

- On Linux, The [AMDGPU driver module](https://rocm.docs.amd.com/projects/install-on-linux/en/latest/how-to/docker.html) needs to be installed on the server and, if secure boot is used, the signing key of DKMS [needs to be enrolled in UEFI BIOS](https://wiki.debian.org/SecureBoot)
- The GPU must be supported by ROCm. If it isn't officially supported, you can attempt to use the `HSA_OVERRIDE_GFX_VERSION` environmental variable: `HSA_OVERRIDE_GFX_VERSION=<a supported version, e.g. 10.3.0>`. If this doesn't work, you might need to also set `HSA_USE_SVM=0`.
- The ROCm image is quite large and requires at least 35GiB of free disk space. However, pulling later updates to the service through Docker will generally only amount to a few hundred megabytes as the rest will be cached.
- This backend is new and may experience some issues. For example, GPU power consumption can be higher than usual after running inference, even if the machine learning service is idle. In this case, it will only go back to normal after being idle for 5 minutes (configurable with the [MACHINE_LEARNING_MODEL_TTL](/install/environment-variables) setting).
- MIGraphX is a new backend for AMD cards, which compiles models at runtime. As such, the first few inferences will be slow.

#### OpenVINO

- Integrated GPUs are more likely to experience issues than discrete GPUs, especially for older processors or servers with low RAM.
- Ensure the server's kernel version is new enough to use the device for hardware acceleration.
- Expect higher RAM usage when using OpenVINO compared to CPU processing.

#### OpenVINO-WSL

- Ensure your container can access the /dev/dri directory, you can verify this by doing `docker exec -t immich_machine_learning ls -la /dev/dri`. If this is not the case execute `getent group render` and `getent group video` on the WSL host, then add those groups to hwaccel.ml.yaml
  ```yaml
  openvino-wsl:
    devices:
      - /dev/dri:/dev/dri
      - /dev/dxg:/dev/dxg
    volumes:
      - /dev/bus/usb:/dev/bus/usb
      - /usr/lib/wsl:/usr/lib/wsl
    group_add:
      - 44 # Replace this number with the number you found with getent group video
      - 992 # Replace this number with the number you found with getent group render
  ```

#### RKNN

- You must have a supported Rockchip SoC: only RK3566, RK3568, RK3576 and RK3588 are supported at this moment.
- Make sure you have the appropriate linux kernel driver installed
  - This is usually pre-installed on the device vendor's Linux images
- RKNPU driver V0.9.8 or later must be available in the host server
  - You may confirm this by running `cat /sys/kernel/debug/rknpu/version` to check the version
- Optional: Configure your `.env` file, see [environment variables](/install/environment-variables) for RKNN specific settings
  - In particular, setting `MACHINE_LEARNING_RKNN_THREADS` to 2 or 3 can _dramatically_ improve performance for RK3576 and RK3588 compared to the default of 1, at the expense of multiplying the amount of RAM each model uses by that amount.

# Monitoring

## Overview

Immich provides a variety of performance metrics to allow for local monitoring and insights. This integration is primarily in the form of Prometheus metrics. However, exporting traces is also possible due to the use of OpenTelemetry instrumentation.

:::note
This is an opt-in feature intended for you to monitor immich's performance. This data isn't sent anywhere beyond what you've configured.
:::

## Prometheus

Prometheus is a tool that collects metrics from a number of sources you configure. It operates in a "pull" strategy - that is, it periodically requests metrics from each defined source. This means that the source doesn't send anything until it's requested. It also means that the source -- immich, in this case -- has to expose an endpoint for Prometheus to target when it requests metrics.

### Metrics

These metrics come in a variety of forms:

- Counters, which can only increase. Example: the number of times an endpoint has been called.
- Gauges, which can increase or decrease within a certain range. Example: CPU utilization.
- Histograms, where each observation is assigned to a certain number of "buckets". Example: response time, where each bucket is a number of milliseconds. This one is a bit more complicated.
  - Buckets in this case are _cumulative_; that is, an observation is placed not only into the smallest bucket that contains it, but also to all buckets larger than this. For example, if a histogram has three buckets for 1ms, 5ms and 10ms, an observation of 3ms will be bucketed into both 5ms and 10ms.

The metrics in immich are grouped into API (endpoint calls and response times), host (memory and CPU utilization), and IO (internal database queries, image processing, and so on). Each group of metrics can be enabled or disabled independently.

### Configuration

Immich will not expose an endpoint for metrics by default. To enable this endpoint, you can add the `IMMICH_TELEMETRY_INCLUDE=all` environmental variable to your `.env` file. Note that only the server container currently use this variable.

:::tip
`IMMICH_TELEMETRY_INCLUDE=all` enables all metrics. For a more granular configuration you can enumerate the telemetry metrics that should be included as a comma separated list (e.g. `IMMICH_TELEMETRY_INCLUDE=repo,api`). Alternatively, you can also exclude specific metrics with `IMMICH_TELEMETRY_EXCLUDE`. For more information refer to the [environment section](/install/environment-variables.md#prometheus).
:::

The next step is to configure a new or existing Prometheus instance to scrape this endpoint. The following steps assume that you do not have an existing Prometheus instance, but the steps will be similar either way.

You can start by defining a Prometheus service in the Compose file:

```yaml
immich-prometheus:
  container_name: immich_prometheus
  ports:
    # this exposes the default port for Prometheus so you can interact with it
    - 9090:9090
  image: prom/prometheus
  volumes:
    # the Prometheus configuration file - a barebones one is provided to get started
    - ./prometheus.yml:/etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml
    # a named volume defined in the bottom of the Compose file; it can also be a mounted folder
    - prometheus-data:/prometheus
```

You will also need to add `prometheus-data` to the list of volumes in the bottom of the Compose file:

```yaml
volumes:
  model-cache:
  prometheus-data:
```

The last piece is the [configuration file][prom-file]. This file defines (among other things) the sources Prometheus should target. Download it and place it in the same folder as the Compose file.

:::tip
The provided file is just a starting point. There are a ton of ways to configure Prometheus, so feel free to experiment!
:::

After bringing down the containers with `docker compose down` and back up with `docker compose up -d`, a Prometheus instance will now collect metrics from the immich server and microservices containers. Note that we didn't need to expose any new ports for these containers - the communication is handled in the internal Docker network.

:::note
To see exactly what metrics are made available, you can additionally add `8081:8081` (API metrics) and `8082:8082` (microservices metrics) to the immich_server container's ports.
Visiting the `/metrics` endpoint for these services will show the same raw data that Prometheus collects.
To configure these ports see [`IMMICH_API_METRICS_PORT` & `IMMICH_MICROSERVICES_METRICS_PORT`](/install/environment-variables/#general).
:::

### Usage

So after setting up Prometheus, how do you actually view the metrics? The simplest way is to use Prometheus directly. Visiting Prometheus will show you a web UI where you can search for and visualize metrics. You can also view the status of your data sources and configure settings, but this is beyond the scope of this guide.

## Grafana

For a dedicated tool with nice presentation, you can use Grafana instead. This connects to Prometheus (and possibly other sources) for sophisticated data visualization.

Setting up Grafana is similar to Prometheus. You can add a service for it:

```yaml
immich-grafana:
  container_name: immich_grafana
  command: ['./run.sh', '-disable-reporting'] # this is to disable Grafana's telemetry
  ports:
    - 3000:3000
  image: grafana/grafana
  volumes:
    # stores your pretty dashboards and panels
    - grafana-data:/var/lib/grafana
```

And add another volume for it:

```yaml
volumes:
  model-cache:
  prometheus-data:
  grafana-data:
```

After bringing down the services and back up again, you can now visit Grafana to view your metrics. On the first login, enter `admin` for both username and password and update your password. You can then go to the settings and add a data source with `http://immich-prometheus:9090` to point Grafana to your Prometheus instance.

## Structured Logging

In addition to Prometheus metrics, Immich supports structured JSON logging which is ideal for log aggregation systems like Grafana Loki, ELK Stack, Datadog, Splunk, and others.

### Configuration

By default, Immich outputs human-readable console logs. To enable JSON logging, set the `IMMICH_LOG_FORMAT` environment variable:

```bash
IMMICH_LOG_FORMAT=json
```

:::tip
The default is `IMMICH_LOG_FORMAT=console` for human-readable logs with colors during development. For production deployments using log aggregation, use `IMMICH_LOG_FORMAT=json`.
:::

### JSON Log Format

When enabled, logs are output in structured JSON format:

```json
{"level":"log","pid":36,"timestamp":1766533331507,"message":"Initialized websocket server","context":"WebsocketRepository"}
{"level":"warn","pid":48,"timestamp":1766533331629,"message":"Unable to open /build/www/index.html, skipping SSR.","context":"ApiService"}
{"level":"error","pid":36,"timestamp":1766533331690,"message":"Failed to load plugin immich-core:","context":"Error"}
```

This format includes:

- `level`: Log level (log, warn, error, etc.)
- `pid`: Process ID
- `timestamp`: Unix timestamp in milliseconds
- `message`: Log message
- `context`: Service or component that generated the log

For more information on log formats, see [`IMMICH_LOG_FORMAT`](/install/environment-variables.md#general).

This includes being able to update their profile, toggle certain feature, generate API keys, manage the logged in devices, a view of account usage statistics, and more. You can access the [user settings](https://my.immich.app/user-settings) by clicking on the user icon on the top right corner of the screen and selecting the `Account Settings` option.
--- :::tip Reset Password The admin can reset a user password through the [User Management](/administration/user-management.mdx) screen. ::: :::tip Reset Admin Password The admin password can be reset using a [Server Command](/administration/server-commands.md) :::

# XMP Sidecars Immich supports XMP sidecar files — external `.xmp` files that store metadata for an image or video in XML format. During the metadata extraction job Immich will read & import metadata from `.xmp` files, and during the Sidecar Write job it will _write_ metadata back to `.xmp`. :::tip Tools like Lightroom, Darktable, digiKam and other applications can also be configured to write changes to `.xmp` files, in order to avoid modifying the original file. ::: ## Metadata Fields Immich does not support _all_ metadata fields. Below is a table showing what fields Immich can _read_ and _write_. It's important to note that writes do not replace the entire file contents, but are merged together with any existing fields. :::info Immich automatically queues a Sidecar Write job after editing the description, rating, or updating tags. ::: | Metadata | Immich writes to XMP | Immich reads from XMP | | --------------- | ------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | **Description** | `dc:description`, `tiff:ImageDescription` | `dc:description`, `tiff:ImageDescription` | | **Rating** | `xmp:Rating` | `xmp:Rating` | | **DateTime** | `exif:DateTimeOriginal`, `photoshop:DateCreated` | In prioritized order:
`exif:SubSecDateTimeOriginal`
`exif:DateTimeOriginal`
`xmp:SubSecCreateDate`
`xmp:CreateDate`
`xmp:CreationDate`
`xmp:MediaCreateDate`
`xmp:SubSecMediaCreateDate`
`xmp:DateTimeCreated` | | **Location** | `exif:GPSLatitude`, `exif:GPSLongitude` | `exif:GPSLatitude`, `exif:GPSLongitude` | | **Tags** | `digiKam:TagsList` | In prioritized order:
`digiKam:TagsList`
`lr:HierarchicalSubject`
`IPTC:Keywords` | :::note All other fields (e.g. `Creator`, `Source`, IPTC, Lightroom edits) remain in the `.xmp` file and are **not searchable** in Immich. ::: ## File Naming Rules A sidecar must share the base name of the media file: - ✅ `IMG_0001.jpg.xmp` ← preferred - ✅ `IMG_0001.xmp` ← fallback - ❌ `myphoto_meta.xmp` ← not recognized If both `.jpg.xmp` and `.xmp` are present, Immich uses the **`.jpg.xmp`** file. ## CLI Support 1. **Detect** – Immich looks for a `.xmp` file placed next to each media file during upload. 2. **Copy** – Both the media and the sidecar file are copied into Immich’s internal library folder. The sidecar is renamed to match the internal filename template, e.g.: `upload/library//YYYY/YYYY-MM-DD/IMG_0001.jpg` `upload/library//YYYY/YYYY-MM-DD/IMG_0001.jpg.xmp` 3. **Extract** – Selected metadata (title, description, date, rating, tags) is parsed from the sidecar and saved to the database. 4. **Write-back** – If you later update tags, rating, or description in the web UI, Immich will update **both** the database _and_ the copied `.xmp` file to stay in sync. ## External Library (Mounted Folder) Support 1. **Detect** – The `DISCOVER` job automatically associates `.xmp` files that sit next to existing media files in your mounted folder. No files are moved or renamed. 2. **Extract** – Immich reads and saves the same metadata fields from the sidecar to the database. 3. **Write-back** – If Immich has **write access** to the mount, any future metadata edits (e.g., rating or tags) are also written back to the original `.xmp` file on disk. :::danger If the mount is **read-only**, Immich cannot update either the sidecar **or** the database — **metadata edits will silently fail** with no warning see issue [#10538](https://github.com/immich-app/immich/issues/10538) for more details. ::: ## Admin Jobs Immich provides two admin jobs for managing sidecars: | Job | What it does | | ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `DISCOVER` | Finds new `.xmp` files next to media that don’t already have one linked | | `SYNC` | Re-reads existing `.xmp` files and refreshes metadata in the database (e.g. after external edits) | ![Sidecar Admin Jobs](./img/sidecar-jobs.webp)

report.overview: Immich is a self-hosted photo and video backup/management platform (Google Photos alternative) structured as a pnpm+mise monorepo. A NestJS/TypeScript server exposes a REST API and BullMQ background workers on Postgres (pgvector/VectorChord) and Redis, a SvelteKit web app and a Flutter mobile app consume a generated OpenAPI SDK, and a separate Python/FastAPI 'machine-learning' microservice runs ONNX models for CLIP search, facial recognition, and OCR. The stock deployment is four docker-compose services: immich-server (port 2283), immich-machine-learning, valkey (Redis), and a pinned Postgres image with vector extensions.

system_map.summary: The system is a multi-process Node.js backend plus three satellite frontends/services. A supervisor in server/src/main.ts forks an 'api' child process and spawns 'microservices'/'maintenance' worker_threads (ImmichWorker enum), each booting a different Nest module from app.module.ts. The API worker serves REST under /api, static web assets via sirv, and socket.io websockets; the microservices worker runs BullMQ consumers over Redis. Persistence is Postgres accessed through Kysely with a hand-maintained schema (server/src/schema) and generated migrations. A Python FastAPI service (machine-learning/) performs inference, and web/ (SvelteKit) plus mobile/ (Flutter) are the user-facing clients built against a generated SDK in packages/sdk.

claims.claim: server/src/main.ts is the process supervisor: Workers.bootstrap() checks maintenance mode, waits on a Postgres advisory lock (DatabaseLock.MaintenanceOperation via pg_try_advisory_lock), then starts each enabled worker — the API worker via child_process.fork and other workers via worker_threads.Worker.

Three runtime worker types exist: ImmichWorker.Api, ImmichWorker.Maintenance, and ImmichWorker.Microservices; the set to run is configurable via IMMICH_WORKERS_INCLUDE/IMMICH_WORKERS_EXCLUDE env vars parsed in EnvSchema.

app.module.ts defines four Nest modules: ApiModule (controllers + AuthGuard + FileUploadInterceptor), MicroservicesModule (BullMQ + SchedulerRegistry), MaintenanceModule (minimal providers + MaintenanceAuthGuard), and ImmichAdminModule (nest-commander CLI commands).

configureExpress() in app.common.ts wires the HTTP stack: trust proxy settings, helmet from helmet.json, cookieParser, 10mb JSON/urlencoded limits, global 'api' prefix with excludePaths, a custom socket.io WebSocketAdapter, swagger, sirv static serving of the built web app, SSR fallback, compression, and a 24-hour requestTimeout.

Postgres is accessed through Kysely (kysely-postgres-js driver); the schema is declared in code under server/src/schema/tables and migrations live in server/src/schema/migrations managed by @immich/sql-tools CLI scripts (migrations:generate/run/revert).
Redis (valkey image in compose) backs BullMQ queues and the socket.io pub/sub adapter; ConfigRepository.getEnv() builds bull.config, bull.queues, and redis options from environment.

The machine-learning service is a standalone FastAPI app (immich_ml/main.py) exposing GET /ping and POST /predict; it keeps an in-memory ModelCache of ONNX models, runs inference on a ThreadPoolExecutor, and can idle-shutdown after model_ttl seconds.

The web frontend is SvelteKit + Vite + Tailwind 4; in dev it proxies /api, /.well-known/immich, and /custom.css to IMMICH_SERVER_URL (default http://immich-server:2283), and in production the API server serves the static build via sirv.
The mobile app is Flutter/Dart (pubspec sdk '>=3.12.0 <4.0.0', flutter 3.47.2) using riverpod, auto_route, drift sqlite, and a generated openapi package at mobile/generated/openapi.

Standard deployment is docker/docker-compose.yml with services immich-server (port 2283, mounts UPLOAD_LOCATION at /data), immich-machine-learning (model-cache volume), valkey redis, and Postgres 14 image 'postgres:14-vectorchord0.4.3-pgvectors0.2.0'.

The workspace is orchestrated by pnpm (pnpm-workspace.yaml) and mise (mise.toml pins node 24.21.0, pnpm 11.24.0, java, jellyfin-ffmpeg, extism/binaryen toolchains); server scripts are nest build / vitest, web scripts are vite build / vitest.

The OpenAPI spec open-api/immich-openapi-specs.json is generated by booting ApiModule in preview mode and writing the swagger document (server/src/bin/sync-open-api.ts); mise task open-api-typescript runs oazapfts to regenerate packages/sdk/src/fetch-client.ts used by web, cli, and e2e.

An admin CLI ('immich-admin') is dispatched in main() before worker bootstrap: it sets process.title 'immich_admin_cli', forces log level Warn, lazily imports ImmichAdminModule, and runs nest-commander commands such as reset-admin-password, grant-admin, password-login, oauth-login, maintenance-mode, and media-location.

feature_catalog.summary: Feature surface is primarily ~45 Nest controllers registered in controllers/index.ts covering assets, albums, sharing, people/faces, search, libraries, jobs, sync, auth, and admin management. Background processing is expressed as JobName jobs on QueueName queues (thumbnails, metadata, video conversion, face detection/recognition, smart search, OCR, duplicates, library scan, backups, notifications, workflows). Auth supports password login, OAuth/OIDC with backchannel logout, API keys, sessions, PIN codes, and shared-link access. A WASM plugin system (extism) plus user-defined workflows are newer extension-oriented features.

claims.claim: Asset upload/download/thumbnails: AssetMediaController exposes POST /assets (multipart, Permission.AssetUpload, sharedLink allowed, optional x-immich-checksum sha1 dedupe header), GET /assets/:id/original, and GET /assets/:id/thumbnail.
Albums, partner sharing, shared links, stacks, and activities each have dedicated controllers and services (album, partner, shared-link, stack, activity) wired through controllers/index.ts.
Search features split into metadata search and smart (CLIP) search via SearchController + SearchRepository backed by pgvector/VectorChord embeddings produced by the ML service.

People/facial recognition is a job pipeline: JobName.AssetDetectFaces and FacialRecognition run on QueueName.FaceDetection/FacialRecognition and call the ML service's facial-recognition detection+recognition pipeline.
Video features include transcoding (fluent-ffmpeg in media.repository.ts, transcoding.service.ts) and HLS session-based streaming coordinated through Hls* events in the EventMap and hls.service.ts.

External libraries support filesystem watching via chokidar and scanning jobs (LibrarySyncAssets/LibrarySyncFiles/LibraryScanQueueAll); watching is locked to a single microservice instance via a database lock.

Auth features: password login with bcrypt + constant-time dummy-hash compare, OAuth/OIDC with backchannel logout token validation, API keys, sessions with lock/invalidate, and PIN code setup/reset/change.

Admin surface: user-admin.controller, system-config.controller, job.controller/queue.controller for pausing/resuming/cleaning BullMQ queues, database-backup.controller, integrity-admin.controller, and notification-admin.controller.

Delta sync for offline-capable clients is implemented by sync.controller.ts + sync.service.ts + sync-checkpoint.repository.ts (SyncCheckpointRepository), which mobile uses to reconcile local drift DB state.

Notifications and email: notification.service.ts + email.repository.ts render react-email templates from server/src/emails and send via nodemailer; jobs like NotifyUserSignup/NotifyAlbumInvite/NotifyAlbumUpdate run on the notifications queue.

A WASM plugin system loads plugins through @extism/extism with a generic-pool of plugin instances in PluginRepository; exposure is gated by env vars IMMICH_PLUGINS_INSTALL_FOLDER and IMMICH_ALLOW_EXTERNAL_PLUGINS, with a @immich/plugin-sdk workspace package for authors.

Workflows (user automation) exist end-to-end: workflow.controller.ts, workflow.repository.ts, utils/workflow.ts (isMethodCompatible for plugin methods), QueueName.Workflow, and a web /workflows route.

Web routes cover photos, albums, favorites, archive, locked folder, map, memories, people, places, partners, search, sharing, shared-links, tags, trash, user-settings, utilities, workflows, plus admin and auth route groups.

Memories, timeline buckets, map clustering, trash auto-empty, duplicate detection, and OCR are first-class jobs/controllers (memory.controller, timeline.controller, map.controller, trash.controller, duplicate.controller, ocr.service).

data_flow.summary: Data enters through Express controllers guarded by a global AuthGuard that produces an AuthDto (user, session, shared link, or API key context) via AuthService.authenticate. Uploads stream through a custom multer storage engine into StorageCore-managed folders under IMMICH_MEDIA_LOCATION, then asset rows are written through repositories over Kysely and BullMQ jobs drive metadata extraction (exiftool), thumbnail generation (sharp), transcoding (ffmpeg), and ML inference via the FastAPI service. All cross-service coordination goes through a typed EventRepository (emit/onEvent) and websocket pushes to clients; mobile/web pull changes via the sync endpoints and socket.io.

claims.claim: Every HTTP request passes the global AuthGuard: @Authenticated metadata (public/setup/admin/sharedLink/permission) is read via Reflector, then AuthService.authenticate resolves credentials from headers (Authorization bearer, x-api-key), cookies (ImmichCookie), or query params (shared-link key/slug) into request.user.

Upload path: FileUploadInterceptor runs a custom multer storage (_handleFile/_removeFile) that writes assetData/sidecarData fields to a per-user upload folder computed by AssetMediaService.getUploadFolder (StorageCore.getNestedFolder(StorageFolder.Upload, userId, uuid)) with sanitized uuid filenames.

After a successful upload, AssetMediaService.uploadAsset creates the asset row (sha1 checksum column for dedupe), upserts sidecar/exif records, queues JobName.AssetExtractMetadata on the metadataExtraction queue, and emits the AssetCreate event; a Postgres checksum-constraint violation is converted into a DUPLICATE response.

Job transport is BullMQ: services call jobRepository.queue/queueAll (Redis), the microservices worker's per-queue bullmq Worker re-emits each job as a 'JobRun' event, and EventRepository dispatches to the method decorated with matching @OnJob({name, queue}).

Metadata extraction (MetadataService.handleMetadataExtraction) reads the asset, calls exiftool via media/metadata repositories, reverse-geocodes GPS through mapRepository when enabled, upserts exif/tags, and emits AssetMetadataExtracted which downstream services use to queue thumbnail/smart-search/face jobs.

ML inference flows server→HTTP: MachineLearningRepository builds typed pipeline requests (ClipVisualRequest, FacialRecognitionRequest, OcrRequest) and POSTs multipart to the FastAPI /predict endpoint, where get_entries parses the pipeline and ModelCache loads ONNX models.

Database access is repository-per-domain (asset.repository, user.repository, ~55 repositories in repositories/index.ts) over a shared KyselyModule connection; services never hold a Kysely handle directly and reach repos through BaseService.

System configuration is a JSON document stored in Postgres (system_metadata/system_config), loaded through utils/config.ts getConfig/updateConfig, and broadcast via ConfigInit/ConfigValidate/ConfigUpdate events that services consume with @OnEvent (e.g., QueueService.updateConcurrency).

Realtime output uses socket.io: WebSocketAdapter attaches a @socket.io/redis-adapter pub/sub pair so API and microservices processes can both emit; WebsocketRepository.setAuthFn authenticates socket handshakes through AuthService.authenticate.

Storage layout is owned by StorageCore: StorageFolder-based paths (upload, library, thumbs/thumbnails, encoded-video, profile, backups) under IMMICH_MEDIA_LOCATION, with file moves tracked through move.repository so DB paths stay consistent.

API contract flows outward: Nest swagger decorators (@Endpoint, @Authenticated, DTO zod schemas) generate immich-openapi-specs.json, which oazapfts turns into packages/sdk fetch-client consumed by web (@immich/sdk), @immich/cli, e2e, and the mobile generated openapi package.

Mobile state sync is pull-based delta sync: sync.controller exposes stream/checkpoint endpoints backed by SyncRepository + SyncCheckpointRepository so the Flutter app's drift sqlite database can incrementally reconcile server state.

behavior_traces.summary: Key flows were walked end-to-end. Startup goes through a supervisor that gates on a Postgres advisory lock and maintenance mode, then each worker boots its Nest module which emits AppBootstrap to ordered handlers (database migrations first, then storage, then job discovery). The upload flow traverses guard → multer interceptors → controller → service → DB + queue. Background work is decoupled: jobs land in Redis and are executed by the microservices worker via a JobRun event indirection.

claims.claim: Startup trace: main() reads argv → Workers.bootstrap() → isMaintenanceMode() (SystemMetadataKey.MaintenanceMode, tolerates missing table via PostgresError 42P01) → waitForFreeLock() (pg_try_advisory_lock loop, 1s poll) → startWorker() per configured ImmichWorker.

API worker boot trace: workers/api.ts bootstrap() → configureTelemetry() → NestFactory.create(ApiModule, {routeConflictPolicy duplicate:error, routeResolutionStrategy specificity}) → AppRepository.setCloseFn → configureExpress(app, {ssr: ApiService}) which installs middleware, sirv, swagger, and listens on port 2283.

Nest module init trace: BaseModule.onModuleInit → telemetryRepository.setup → queueService.setServices(services) → websocketRepository.setAuthFn(authenticate) → eventRepository.setup({services}) → emit('AppBootstrap'); onModuleDestroy emits AppShutdown and tears down telemetry.

Bootstrap ordering is priority-driven: DatabaseService.onBootstrap (priority -200) checks Postgres version range, manages the vector extension (create/update/drop, reindexVectorsIfNeeded), and runs migrations under DatabaseLock.Migrations unless DB_SKIP_MIGRATIONS; StorageService (-195) and JobService (-190) follow, SystemConfig at +100, PluginSync/PluginLoad at +190/+200.

Job-handler discovery trace: QueueService.onBootstrap (AppBootstrap listener) → jobRepository.setup(services) reflects over every service method, registers those with @OnJob metadata into handlers{}, and throws ImmichStartupError if any JobName value lacks a handler or two handlers claim one job; microservices then startWorkers() and the api worker starts watchWorkers() (30s liveness poll).

Upload trace: POST /api/assets → AuthGuard.canActivate (Permission.AssetUpload, sharedLink ok) → AssetUploadInterceptor/FileUploadInterceptor multer writes file → AssetMediaController.uploadAsset → service.uploadAsset → requireAccess + requireQuota → onBeforeLink for livePhotoVideoId → assetRepository.create → upsertMetadata/upsertFile/upsertExif → jobRepository.queue(AssetExtractMetadata) → eventRepository.emit(AssetCreate) → 201 or 200-on-duplicate.

Metadata extraction trace: microservices bullmq Worker dequeues → eventRepository.emit('JobRun', queueName, job) → JobRepository.run dispatches → MetadataService.handleMetadataExtraction → getExifTags (exiftool) + stat → getDates/getImageDimensions → reverseGeocode if GPS → upsert → downstream AssetMetadataExtracted event queues thumbnails, smart search, and face detection.

Login trace: POST /auth/login → AuthService.login → getConfig(passwordLogin.enabled gate) → userRepository.getByEmail(withPassword) → cryptoRepository.compareBcrypt against user password or LOGIN_DUMMY_HASH for constant-time behavior → createLoginResponse(user, details) issues session + cookies.

Nightly tasks trace: on ConfigInit the non-microservices worker takes DatabaseLock.NightlyJobs, converts config.nightlyTasks.startTime to a cron expression, and registers CronJob.NightlyJobs whose onTick calls handleNightlyJobs(); ConfigUpdate re-schedules it.

Worker crash/restart trace: any worker 'exit' triggers onExit; exitCode ExitCode.AppRestart sets restarting=true and reboots all workers once drained; a non-zero exit otherwise kills the api worker (SIGTERM) if present and exits the supervisor process with the same code.

Websocket connect trace: socket.io handshake → WebSocketAdapter (redis pub/sub adapter) → authFn registered in BaseModule → AuthService.authenticate with uri '/api/socket.io' → WebsocketConnect event emitted with userId.

ML predict trace: POST /predict → get_entries parses multipart 'entries' JSON into InferenceEntry list splitting with/without model deps → run_inference resolves deps (detection output feeds recognition) → model_cache.get + load() (ONNX fallback if other format unsupported) → model.predict in thread pool → ORJSONResponse.

testing_signals.summary: Testing is layered: Vitest unit tests co-located as *.spec.ts in server/src and web/src, a 'medium' tier in server/test/medium that runs against a real Postgres via testcontainers, API-level e2e specs in e2e/ (Vitest + supertest-style SDK calls against a docker-compose stack), and Playwright browser/UI/maintenance projects. CI (.github/workflows/test.yml) shards jobs per changed directory. Coverage is configured but explicitly excludes some files, and several infra-heavy areas (storage.core is covered, but websocket/adapter and plugin internals have thin coverage).

claims.claim: Server unit tests run with vitest config test/vitest.config.mjs: name 'server:unit', globals on, include 'src/**/*.spec.ts', swc transform, v8 coverage scoped to src/cores, src/services, src/utils, src/sql-tools.

A separate medium tier (test/vitest.config.medium.mjs, 'pnpm test:medium') runs integration-style specs in server/test/medium/specs (exif, repositories, services, sync, workflow) with a globalSetup.ts, using testcontainers (devDependency) for real Postgres.

Tests use a factory/stub pattern: server/test/factories/*.factory.ts (asset, auth, user, session, shared-link, person, etc.) plus server/test/fixtures/*.stub.ts and small.factory.ts/medium.factory.ts builders.
Most controllers and services have co-located .spec.ts files (e.g., asset-media.controller.spec.ts, auth.service.spec.ts, queue.service.spec.ts) — the dominant convention is one spec per source file.

e2e/ runs Vitest API specs (src/specs/{server,web,maintenance} covering api, cli, immich-admin) and three Playwright projects (web, ui, maintenance) driven by playwright.config.ts against a docker-compose stack (e2e/docker-compose.yml).
Web unit tests run via vitest inside vite.config.ts: name 'web:unit', happy-dom environment, svelteTesting plugin, setup file src/test-data/setup.ts, TZ=UTC.

CI test.yml gates on a pre-job change filter and runs: server unit+lint (mise //server:ci-unit), server medium tests, web lint+unit, cli unit on linux+windows, e2e server-cli and e2e web matrices on ubuntu amd64+arm64 with docker compose up and artifacted docker logs/playwright reports.
check-openapi.yml enforces that the generated spec is in sync with the code and migration-order.yml verifies migration ordering — both are dedicated CI workflows.
machine-learning has pytest tests (test_main.py, conftest.py) and a locustfile.py for load testing the predict endpoint.
Mobile has a Flutter test/ tree and integration_test/ directory; mobile CI is exercised through build-mobile.yml rather than the main test workflow.

Coverage config explicitly excludes api.service.ts and microservices.service.ts from instrumentation, and files like websocket.adapter.ts, plugin.service.ts, and several controllers have no co-located spec — thin spots in otherwise high coverage.

risk_map.summary: Security-sensitive surface concentrates on file upload/disk IO, auth token handling, subprocess media tooling, and the WASM plugin host. The multer storage engine writes user-supplied bytes to predictable uuid paths, ffmpeg/exiftool process untrusted media, and extism plugins run third-party WASM gated by env vars. Operational risks include a 24h request timeout, trust-proxy assumptions, startup-time migrations under an advisory lock, and a supervisor that kills the whole process on worker failure. Several safety rails exist (mandatory @Authenticated, duplicate-job startup validation, constant-time login compare) but are themselves fragile coupling points.

claims.claim: File upload writes untrusted bytes through a custom multer _handleFile to disk paths derived from StorageCore folders; filenames are sanitized via sanitize-filename and uuid-based, but the interceptor runs before controller validation, so malformed multipart payloads hit the FS layer early.

express 'trust proxy' is set to ['loopback', ...network.trustedProxies] from IMMICH_TRUSTED_PROXIES; clientIp used in login logging/GetLoginDetails depends on this being correct — misconfiguration enables IP spoofing in audit logs and rate-sensitive paths.
server.requestTimeout is set to 24 hours (24*60*60*1000) to support huge uploads/downloads; combined with 10mb JSON body limits this leaves long-lived socket exposure on the API port.

Password auth uses bcrypt compare against LOGIN_DUMMY_HASH when the email is unknown (constant-time anti-enumeration) — the dummy hash constant lives in constants.ts and weakening/removing it would reopen user enumeration.

Shared-link access is authorized via query parameters (key/slug) declared with ApiQuery in the @Authenticated decorator, meaning bearer-equivalent secrets can appear in URLs, access logs, and referrers.

Media processing shells out to ffmpeg/ffprobe (fluent-ffmpeg) and exiftool-vendored on user-uploaded files; media.repository.ts builds ffmpeg calls with niceness 10 — a large blast radius if argument handling or the bundled jellyfin-ffmpeg is compromised.

The plugin host instantiates extism WASM plugins pooled via generic-pool and calls plugin methods by name; external plugin installation is env-gated (IMMICH_ALLOW_EXTERNAL_PLUGINS) and mis-set values expand supply-chain surface.

Startup is stateful and lock-coupled: the supervisor busy-polls pg_try_advisory_lock(MaintenanceOperation), DatabaseService runs migrations under DatabaseLock.Migrations, and nightly jobs require DatabaseLock.NightlyJobs — stuck locks or split-brain DBs can wedge boot or scheduling.

Any non-zero worker exit kills the API child (SIGTERM) and exits the supervisor with that code — a crash in a background job can take down the whole API unless orchestrated restart policies compensate.

Every route must declare @Authenticated() or AuthGuard throws at request time ('Route X does not declare @Authenticated()'); this is a strong default-deny but means a missing decorator yields runtime 500s rather than compile errors.

Library watching uses chokidar over admin-configured filesystem paths and writes discovered files into the managed tree; a hostile or malformed library path expands file-IO reach beyond the media root.

Dev/test convenience defaults embed credentials: DB_URL defaults to postgres://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/immich in migration scripts and sync-open-api.ts hardcodes the same DSN — fine for local dev but a footgun if reused.

Postgres's 65535 bind-parameter limit is worked around via the @Chunked decorator (DATABASE_PARAMETER_CHUNK_SIZE 65_500); repository methods handling ID sets rely on authors remembering to decorate — a missed site yields runtime driver errors on large batches.
Mobile pins a git dependency (native_video_player) to a commit ref and consumes a generated openapi package — both are supply-chain and drift-sensitive integration points.

extension_points.summary: The codebase is organized around explicit registries: controllers/index.ts, services/index.ts, repositories/index.ts, commands/index.ts, plus decorator-driven registration (@OnJob, @OnEvent, @Endpoint, @Authenticated). Adding an endpoint means a controller method + zod DTO + index registration; adding a job means enum entries + @OnJob handler (enforced at startup). A WASM plugin system via @immich/plugin-sdk and workflows provide runtime extensibility, and the OpenAPI→SDK codegen pipeline propagates API changes to all clients.

claims.claim: New HTTP endpoints plug in via a controller class added to the controllers array in controllers/index.ts; the ApiModule mounts every entry under the global /api prefix.

New background jobs require: a JobName enum member, a QueueName choice, and a method decorated @OnJob({name, queue}) on a service — jobRepository.setup validates complete coverage at boot and throws ImmichStartupError for missing or duplicate handlers.

New domain events plug in via the typed EventMap in event.repository.ts plus @OnEvent({name, priority, server, workers}) on service methods; BootstrapEventPriority documents ordering constraints for bootstrap handlers.
New services extend BaseService (which injects all ~55 repositories) and must be added to services/index.ts so queueService.setServices and eventRepository.setup can discover their decorated methods.
New repositories are classes added to repositories/index.ts and BASE_SERVICE_DEPENDENCIES so every service receives them positionally through BaseService's constructor.

WASM plugins are a first-class extension point: authors build against @immich/plugin-sdk (host-functions.ts, sdk.ts), plugins install under IMMICH_PLUGINS_INSTALL_FOLDER, are pooled/executed by PluginRepository via extism, and their methods/templates surface through plugin.controller and workflow compatibility checks.
Admin CLI commands plug in via nest-commander Command classes registered in commands/index.ts (commandsAndQuestions) and run under ImmichAdminModule when invoked as 'immich-admin'.

API versioning/documentation is decorator-driven: @Endpoint({summary, history: new HistoryBuilder().added('vX').beta('vY')}) emits custom swagger extensions (x-immich-history/state) that feed the generated spec — deprecations flow automatically via ApiTag.Deprecated.

Request/response validation is nestjs-zod: DTOs are zod schemas (e.g., EnvSchema, QueueNameSchema) validated globally by ZodValidationPipe and serialized by ZodSerializerInterceptor registered as APP_PIPE/APP_INTERCEPTOR.

DB schema changes plug in through sql-tools: table classes in server/src/schema/tables with Column/trigger decorators (PrimaryGeneratedUuidV7Column, UpdatedAtTrigger), functions in schema/functions.ts, then 'pnpm migrations:generate' diffs into schema/migrations with an ORDER file.

Client surface extends via codegen: edit DTOs/controllers → run sync-open-api.ts to refresh immich-openapi-specs.json → mise task open-api-typescript regenerates packages/sdk fetch-client used by web/cli/e2e; mobile consumes a generated dart openapi package.
Web features plug in as SvelteKit routes under web/src/routes/(user)/... with shared components/stores/managers in web/src/lib, all typed against @immich/sdk.
Bull queues self-register: ConfigRepository builds RegisterQueueOptions for every QueueName value (bull.queues) so adding a QueueName enum member automatically creates the queue without extra wiring.

agent_handoff.summary: This is a large, convention-heavy monorepo — change one layer and the generated artifacts (OpenAPI spec, SDK, migrations, mobile client) must be regenerated and kept in sync or CI fails. Server code follows strict layering (controller → service → repository → Kysely) with decorator-driven registration that will fail loudly at startup if misconfigured. Tests are fast to run per-package but e2e/medium tiers need Docker. Read the bootstrap and decorator machinery before editing anything structural.

claims.claim: Read first (server): server/src/main.ts (supervisor), server/src/app.module.ts (module wiring), server/src/enum.ts (all JobName/QueueName/ImmichWorker/Permission values), server/src/decorators.ts (@OnJob/@OnEvent/@Endpoint/@Chunked), server/src/services/base.service.ts (repository injection convention).

Convention: controllers stay thin — they take @Auth() AuthDto + DTOs and delegate to a service; every handler must declare @Authenticated() (defaults to authenticated; use {public:true} or {sharedLink:true} variants) or the guard throws.
Convention: authorization inside services goes through this.requireAccess({auth, permission, ids}) / checkAccess backed by access.repository.ts — don't hand-roll ownership checks.

Adding a job is a startup-validated contract: new JobName without an @OnJob handler (or a duplicate handler) aborts boot with ImmichStartupError — always add enum + decorated method + ensure the service is in services/index.ts.

API changes must be followed by regeneration: sync-open-api.ts writes the spec, 'mise run open-api-typescript' rebuilds packages/sdk, and the check-openapi CI workflow fails if the committed spec drifts.

Schema changes: edit table classes under server/src/schema/tables, then 'pnpm migrations:generate' (sql-tools against DB_URL); ordering is enforced by schema/migrations/ORDER and the migration-order.yml workflow — see docs/docs/developer/database-migrations.md.

Test commands: server unit 'pnpm test' (vitest, no DB needed), 'pnpm test:medium' (needs Docker for testcontainers), e2e 'pnpm test'/'test:web' in e2e/ (needs docker compose up), web 'pnpm test'. Lint gates are strict: eslint --max-warnings 0 plus prettier checks.

Known trap: services get repositories positionally through BaseService — adding a repository means updating repositories/index.ts AND the BASE_SERVICE_DEPENDENCIES tuple AND the constructor AND BaseService.create in the same order, or DI silently misaligns.

Known trap: file paths on disk must go through StorageCore/StorageRepository helpers (StorageFolder layout, media location from IMMICH_MEDIA_LOCATION) — never construct storage paths ad hoc, and DB-stored paths are updated via MoveRepository.

Known trap: long-running requests are normal (24h requestTimeout, streaming uploads/downloads via sendFile/ImmichFileResponse) — avoid buffering whole files in memory and prefer the ImmichFileResponse pattern for binary responses.
Environment config is centralized: add new env vars to EnvSchema in dtos/env.dto.ts and surface them via ConfigRepository.getEnv(); never read process.env inside services.

Toolchain is pinned by mise (node 24.21.0, pnpm 11.24.0, java 21 for openapi-generator, extism/binaryen for plugins, jellyfin-ffmpeg for transcoding tests) — use 'mise run //server:ci-unit' style tasks to match CI rather than raw pnpm where possible.

report.agent_prompt:
You are working in the Immich monorepo (pnpm + mise, v3.2.0), a self-hosted photo/video backup platform. Architecture: a NestJS 12/TypeScript server in server/ exposes a REST API (Express 5, global /api prefix) and runs BullMQ background workers; a SvelteKit app in web/ and a Flutter app in mobile/ are the clients; a Python FastAPI ONNX inference service lives in machine-learning/. Standard deploy is docker-compose: immich-server:2283, immich-machine-learning, valkey (Redis), Postgres 14 with VectorChord/pgvector.

Server boot model: server/src/main.ts is a supervisor that forks an 'api' child process and spawns 'microservices'/'maintenance' worker_threads (ImmichWorker enum). Each worker boots a Nest module from src/app.module.ts. Module init emits a typed 'AppBootstrap' event; handlers ordered by BootstrapEventPriority run DB migrations (under advisory lock), storage setup, then job-handler discovery.

Conventions you must follow:
- Controllers (src/controllers/, registered in controllers/index.ts) are thin: @Authenticated() is REQUIRED on every route (options: public, admin, sharedLink, permission: Permission.X). Use @Endpoint({summary, history: new HistoryBuilder()...}) for docs. DTOs are zod schemas (nestjs-zod validates globally).
- Services (src/services/, in services/index.ts) extend BaseService, which injects ~55 repositories POSITIONALLY — if you add a repository, update repositories/index.ts, BASE_SERVICE_DEPENDENCIES, the constructor, and BaseService.create in identical order. Authz inside services: this.requireAccess({auth, permission, ids}).
- Background jobs: add JobName + pick QueueName (enum.ts) + a method with @OnJob({name, queue}). Startup fails if a JobName has no handler. Queue via this.jobRepository.queue/queueAll.
- Events: extend EventMap in repositories/event.repository.ts, subscribe with @OnEvent({name, priority, server, workers}).
- Files on disk: only via StorageCore/StorageRepository paths (StorageFolder.* under IMMICH_MEDIA_LOCATION); DB path updates via MoveRepository.
- Env vars: add to EnvSchema in dtos/env.dto.ts; read via ConfigRepository.getEnv(). Never touch process.env in services.
- Large ID lists in queries need @Chunked (65535 bind-param limit).

After API changes regenerate contracts: run server/src/bin/sync-open-api.ts (or the repo task) to refresh open-api/immich-openapi-specs.json, then 'mise run open-api-typescript' to rebuild packages/sdk (web, cli, e2e consume it; mobile uses a generated dart openapi package). check-openapi.yml fails on drift.

DB changes: edit src/schema/tables (+ functions.ts), then 'pnpm migrations:generate' in server/ (needs a Postgres at DB_URL); ORDER file and migration-order.yml enforce sequence.

Testing: server unit 'pnpm test' in server/ (vitest, src/**/*.spec.ts, no DB); 'pnpm test:medium' needs Docker (testcontainers). e2e/ has vitest API specs and Playwright projects requiring docker compose up. Web: 'pnpm test' (happy-dom). Lint is strict: eslint --max-warnings 0 + prettier. Use mise tasks (mise.toml pins node 24.21.0, pnpm 11.24.0) to match CI.

Traps: worker non-zero exit kills the API process; requestTimeout is 24h (stream, don't buffer); shared-link secrets travel in query params; login compare must stay constant-time (LOGIN_DUMMY_HASH); plugin loading is env-gated (IMMICH_ALLOW_EXTERNAL_PLUGINS); mobile pubspec pins git deps.
